Part C: Cloning and sequence verification

Because sequence variation may exist between published reference assemblies and the WT strain used, the genomic sequence of the WT strain should be used as the reference when genotyping edited clones. The E. gracilis genome typically contains 2–3 copies of each gene, and these copies have high sequence similarity. In this genotyping experiment, as sequences that commonly recognize these homologous genes were used, the resulting PCR products must be cloned into a vector to sequence individual clones and distinguish them. If the PCR fragment is too short and does not contain regions that can differentiate among the homologous sequences, primers should be redesigned to amplify a longer region that includes the deletion. PCR should then be performed again to obtain a fragment suitable for cloning. Direct sequencing of PCR products is often difficult due to the presence of mixed amplicons from the different homologous genes. Therefore, it is preferable to use a kit that allows direct cloning of PCR products (e.g., pJET, CloneJET PCR Cloning Kit, and Thermo Fisher Scientific). Please follow the instructions provided in the original protocol, with the option to scale down the reaction if necessary.
Use deionized distilled water in all the recipes and protocol steps.

steps.title: Prepare KH liquid medium and culture cells
steps.instruction: Prepare KH liquid medium (pH 3.5 or 5.5) by dissolving the KH base components (0.5 g L⁻¹ l‑Arginine·HCl, 0.3 g L⁻¹ l‑Aspartic acid, 12 g L⁻¹ d‑Glucose, 4 g L⁻¹ l‑Glutamic acid, 0.3 g L⁻¹ Glycine, 0.05 g L⁻¹ l‑Histidine·HCl·H₂O, 6.5 g L⁻¹ dl‑Malic acid, 0.5 g L⁻¹ Trisodium citrate·2H₂O, 0.1 g L⁻¹ Disodium succinate, 0.5 g L⁻¹ (NH₄)₂SO₄, 0.25 g L⁻¹ NH₄HCO₃, 0.25 g L⁻¹ KH₂PO₄, 0.12 g L⁻¹ CaCO₃, 0.6 g L⁻¹ MgCO₃·4Mg(OH)₂·xH₂O) in de‑ionised water, add KH trace metal stock A (10 g L⁻¹ EDTA‑2Na, 10 g L⁻¹ (NH₄)₂Fe(SO₄)₂·6H₂O → final 50 mg L⁻¹ each) and KH trace metal stock B (3.6 g L⁻¹ MnSO₄·5H₂O, 5 g L⁻¹ ZnSO₄·7H₂O, 0.8 g L⁻¹ (NH₄)₆Mo₇O₂₄·4H₂O, 0.24 g L⁻¹ CuSO₄·5H₂O, 0.12 g L⁻¹ H₃BO₃, 0.1 g L⁻¹ CoSO₄·7H₂O, 0.1 g L⁻¹ NiSO₄·6H₂O, 0.1 g L⁻¹ NH₄VO₃ → final concentrations as listed) and KH vitamin stock C (0.5 g L⁻¹ thiamine·HCl, 1 mg L⁻¹ cyanocobalamin → final 2.5 mg L⁻¹ and 0.005 mg L⁻¹ respectively). Adjust pH to 3.5 (or 5.5 for solid medium) with KOH, bring volume to 1 L, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min, store at room temperature in the dark ≤3 months. Sterilise 100 mL Erlenmeyer flasks (e.g., CTE33, Iwaki) with silicone plugs. Inoculate E. gracilis strain Z (NIES‑48) into 50 mL KH liquid medium pH 3.5, incubate in a 26 °C incubator with continuous white light at 50 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, shaking on a rotary shaker placed inside the incubator. Culture for 4 days (Days 1‑4) to reach logarithmic phase; these cells will be used for electroporation.

steps.title: Design and order sgRNA oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Using the E. gracilis genome, design two non‑overlapping 20‑nt target sequences (sgRNA #1 and sgRNA #2) that delete the region of interest and that are present in all homologous copies. Verify each 20‑nt sequence against the whole genome to avoid off‑targets. Order four single‑stranded DNA oligos: a₁ (sgRNA #1 target, OPC‑purified), a₂ (sgRNA #2 target, OPC‑purified), b and c (crRNA/tracrRNA scaffold parts, OPC‑purified).

steps.title: Amplify sgRNA template by PCR and purify
steps.instruction: Set up a high‑fidelity PCR (e.g., Tks Gflex DNA Polymerase, Takara Bio) in 0.2 mL PCR tubes using purified oligos a₁, a₂, b, and c as primers to generate the sgRNA DNA template (>100 ng). Run the PCR product on a 0.5 × TAE agarose gel (1 %–1.5 % agarose) stained with FluoroVue DNA Fluorescent Staining Dye. Visualise with a LED‑Transilluminator, excise the correct band, and purify using a NucleoSpin Gel and PCR Clean‑up Kit. Quantify the purified template with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.

steps.title: In‑vitro transcribe and purify sgRNAs
steps.instruction: Using the CUGA7 sgRNA Synthesis Kit (cat. no. 314‑08691, Nippon Gene), combine 100 ng purified template, 5 µL 5× Transcription Buffer, 2 µL 0.1 M DTT, 5 µL NTP mix, RNase‑free water to 20 µL, and 1 µL CUGA7 Enzyme Solution. Incubate at 37 °C for 2 h (as per kit). Treat the reaction with 1 µL DNase I (RNase‑free) at 37 °C for 15 min. Bind the RNA to the provided spin column, wash, and elute sgRNA in RNase‑free water. Measure concentration; the kit yields 2000–4000 ng µL⁻¹. Aliquot and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Assemble Cas9‑sgRNA ribonucleoprotein complexes
steps.instruction: Thaw Alt‑R S.p. Cas9 Nuclease V3 (Integrated DNA Technologies) on ice. Mix Cas9 protein with each sgRNA (sgRNA #1 and sgRNA #2) at the ratio recommended by the manufacturer (typically 1 µg Cas9 with 1 µg sgRNA) in a low‑binding tube. Incubate at room temperature for 10 min to allow RNP formation. Keep the RNP mixture on ice until electroporation.

steps.title: Prepare electroporation buffer and reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare Cramer‑Myers (CM) liquid medium (pH 5.5) by dissolving CM base components (1 g L⁻¹ (NH₄)₂HPO₄, 1 g L⁻¹ KH₂PO₄, 0.2 g L⁻¹ MgSO₄·7H₂O, 0.02 g L⁻¹ CaCl₂) in distilled water, add CM trace metal stock A and vitamin stock B (1 mL L⁻¹ each), adjust pH to 5.5 with 10 % (v/v) H₂SO₄, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min. Filter‑sterilise a 0.3 M sucrose solution (51.3 g sucrose in 500 mL water, filter 0.2 µm). Keep both solutions at room temperature (sucrose) or 4 °C (CM) until use. Also have 5 M NaCl stock (14.6 g NaCl in 50 mL water, autoclave) ready for washing steps.

steps.title: Harvest log‑phase cells and wash
steps.instruction: On Day 5, collect log‑phase E. gracilis from the KH liquid culture (pH 3.5). Count cells with a Thoma hemocytometer and transfer ~1 × 10⁶ cells into a 15 mL sterile centrifuge tube. Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 3 min, discard supernatant, and wash the pellet once with 10 mL CM liquid medium (pH 5.5) containing 0.3 M sucrose. Centrifuge again (1,000 × g, 3 min) and resuspend the pellet in 100 µL CM medium (pH 5.5) with sucrose.

steps.title: Electroporate cells with Cas9 RNPs
steps.instruction: Add the pre‑assembled Cas9‑sgRNA RNP mixture (containing both sgRNA #1 and sgRNA #2) to the 100 µL cell suspension. Transfer the 100 µL mixture into a 2‑mm gap electroporation cuvette (e.g., EC‑002S, NEPAGENE). Electroporate using the previously optimised settings for E. gracilis (e.g., 1.5 kV, 25 µF, 200 Ω – exact parameters as determined in the lab). Immediately add 2 mL pre‑warmed KH liquid medium (pH 3.5) to the cuvette, gently mix, and transfer the entire volume to a sterile 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Recover electroporated cells in liquid medium
steps.instruction: Incubate the recovered cells at 26 °C under continuous white light (50 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) with shaking on a rotary shaker for 30 min to allow membrane repair before plating.

steps.title: Plate cells in top agar on solid medium
steps.instruction: Prepare KH top agar (0.2 % w/v agar in KH liquid medium, pH 3.5): add 1 g agar powder to 500 mL KH medium (pH 3.5), autoclave 121 °C for 20 min, keep molten at 42–45 °C. Mix 200 µL of recovered cell suspension with 800 µL molten top agar, vortex briefly, and pour the mixture onto pre‑cooled KH solid plates (0.8 % agar, pH 5.5: 4 g agar in 500 mL KH medium pH 5.5, autoclaved, cooled to ~55 °C before pouring). Allow plates to solidify at room temperature, then invert and incubate at 26 °C, 50 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ white light.

steps.title: Incubate plates for colony development
steps.instruction: Incubate the plated cells for 7–9 days (Days 7‑14) until isolated colonies become visible. Record colony appearance dates; colonies are ready for genotyping after ~10 days of growth on agar.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA by alkaline lysis
steps.instruction: Pick an individual colony with a sterile toothpick, transfer into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 100 µL 50 mM NaOH (prepared by dissolving 0.2 g NaOH in 100 mL water, filter‑sterilised). Vortex briefly and incubate at 95 °C for 10 min (or at room temperature for 5 min if heat block unavailable). Add 10 µL 1 M Tris·HCl (pH 8.0, prepared by dissolving 60.55 g Tris base in 400 mL water, adjust pH to 8.0 with HCl, bring to 500 mL) to neutralise. Mix and store the crude DNA on ice; this preparation can be used directly for PCR.

steps.title: Perform first PCR to detect deletions
steps.instruction: Set up a 25 µL PCR using OmniPCR Supermix (OnePCR Ultra) with Fluorescent Dye, 0.5 µM each of the primer pair flanking the expected deletion region (1st PCR primers), 2 µL crude DNA, and nuclease‑free water to volume. Run the thermal cycler (e.g., Veriti 96‑well) with the recommended cycling conditions (initial denaturation 95 °C 3 min; 30 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min). Load 5 µL of PCR product on a 1 %–1.5 % agarose gel in 0.5 × TAE, alongside a 500 bp DNA ladder (FluoroDye DNA Fluorescent Loading Dye Green). Visualise under LED‑Transilluminator. A shorter band than the wild‑type size indicates a deletion.

steps.title: Perform second PCR to confirm wild‑type loss
steps.instruction: Repeat the PCR using the primer pair that amplifies within the region expected to be deleted (2nd PCR primers). Use the same reaction mix and cycling conditions as the first PCR. Run the products on a 1 %–1.5 % agarose gel as above. Absence of a band indicates successful deletion of the target region.

steps.title: Analyze PCR gels for editing
steps.instruction: Compare the first‑PCR gel to the wild‑type control: colonies showing a band shorter than the wild‑type amplicon are candidate edits. Verify that the same colonies lack a band in the second‑PCR gel. Record colonies that satisfy both criteria for downstream cloning.

steps.title: Clone PCR products and sequence clones
steps.instruction: Purify the first‑PCR product from each positive colony using a magnetic‑bead‑based cleanup (or ExoSAP‑IT if the polymerase lacks fluorescent dye). Ligate the purified fragment into a pJET CloneJET PCR Cloning Kit vector according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Transform competent E. coli, plate on selective agar, and incubate overnight at 37 °C. Pick 15–20 white colonies per original E. gracilis colony, perform colony PCR to confirm insert presence, and purify the PCR product. Submit purified inserts for Sanger sequencing. Ensure that sequencing primers anneal outside the cloned region to obtain the full amplicon.

steps.title: Interpret sequencing results across homologs
steps.instruction: Align each obtained sequence to the reference EgcrtB loci (three copies on chromosome 6). Confirm that the expected deletions and PAM disruptions are present in all homologous copies. If mixed or wild‑type sequences are detected, redesign sgRNAs or primers and repeat the cloning‑sequencing workflow.
